v: Now, Reader, I have told my dream. Now see
if you can make its meaning plain to me,
or to yourself or neighbor. But take heed
not to misread it; for that, instead
of doing good, will only wound and bruise:
from misinterpretation, harm ensues.
Take care, as well, not to be too extreme
in playing with the surface of my dream;
nor let my figures, or similitude,
provoke you into laughter or a feud.
Leave that to boys and fools; but you, instead,
look for the substance of the things I’ve said.
Draw back the curtains, look behind my veil,
turn up my metaphors, and you won’t fail,
if you will seek them there, such things to find
as will be helpful to an honest mind.
Whatever dross you find there, then be bold
to throw away, but still preserve the gold.
What if my gold is wrapped up in its ore?
No one throws out the apple for the core.
But if you cast it all away as vain,
who knows? It may just make me dream again.
